newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai rice futures end mixed in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai rice futures end mixed in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai rice futures ended mixed in slow trading on Thursday, with investors liquidating positions in the September 1996 contract which will begin delivery on Tuesday next week, traders said.
The key September contract ended at an intra-day low of 2,467 yuan ($297) per tonne, but up 26 yuan from Wednesday. It opened at an intra-day high of 2,480.
October fell six yuan to 2,320 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 5,200 tonnes from 105,300.
Traders said stop-loss orders continued to emerge on the market today after yesterday's sharp losses.
"Retail investors holding long positons in the September contract continued to offset because they did not want to take physical goods," one trader said.
Traders said rice futures were likely to fall on Friday, with retail investors selling the September contract.
